key_insight: Agentic AI controllers that orchestrate LLMs and tools should be Bayes-consistent: maintain and update probabilistic beliefs and make decisions by maximizing expected utility, improving decisions under uncertainty compared to ad-hoc heuristics.
problem_solved: Clarifies how to handle decisions under uncertainty in agentic systems (which tool to call, which expert to consult, how much resource to invest) by applying Bayesian decision principles at the control/orchestration layer.
method: Treat the controller as a Bayesian decision-maker: represent uncertainty with priors, update beliefs from LLM outputs and observations, and compute posteriors.
Choose actions (tool calls, expert queries, resource allocations) by maximizing expected utility under the posterior, trading off information gain and task payoff.
Integrate calibration of LLM-provided probabilities and explicit models of tool outcomes to ensure Bayes-consistency across the orchestration loop.
impact: Provides a principled framework for safer, more efficient orchestration of LLMs and tools, enabling better trade-offs between exploration, cost, and task performance—useful for designers of agentic systems and production pipelines.
visual_elements: System diagram: agent loop showing LLMs, tools, observations, Bayesian belief update, and decision/action node.
Flowchart: belief → posterior update → expected-utility computation → action selection (tool/expert/resource).
Heatmap or bar chart: expected utility comparisons between Bayes-consistent vs heuristic orchestration across scenarios (cost, accuracy, latency).
Icon set: calibrated probability gauge, tool-call icon, expert/consult icon, resource budget meter.
paper_title: Position: agentic AI orchestration should be Bayes-consistent
paper_authors: Theodore Papamarkou, Pierre Alquier, Matthias Bauer, Wray Buntine, Andrew Davison
